subject: koala
reasoning:
I'm planning a TypeScript module that builds a stylized koala from primitives using the SDK, sizing it based on real koala proportions and designing it to sit on a tree branch, keeping the code robust and avoiding risky APIs.

Working out the skeleton structure...

Still defining joint positions...

I'll sweep the body along the spine chain itself so it bends naturally, using a radius function returning both sideways width and height to give the koala its wide, round shape, with t=0 at the hips and t=1 near the neck.

Now I'm figuring out the body proportions and leg placement so the koala's feet rest at the floor -- sizing the hip joints, leg length, and radius so the bottom of the body and legs line up at ground level, then planning each leg as a short three-joint chain.

So names ["hipL","kneeL","footL"] with role leg gives the tip joint automatically at the chain's end. For the limb function, lengths map to segment counts and bends define joint-bend directions, like [0,0,1] for a forward knee bend on the koala's legs.

I'm positioning front legs (arms) from shoulder to paw, and back legs from hip to foot, checking that the segment lengths and distances stay consistent with the limb geometry. For the arms I'll bend the elbow backward with [0,0,-1], and build each chain with parent attachment to the spine's chest joint, naming shoulder, elbow, and paw so the tip resolves correctly with three joints total.

Now I'm figuring out the ears -- considering a flattened sphere or a cylinder disc shape attached to the head, oriented sideways with a direction vector so they sit flush against the skull like round koala ears.

For positioning, I'm using the local coordinate words (left, up, forward) to place the ears relative to the head joint, and planning the head itself as a large rounded sphere with a slight forward-up tilt to match the bone's aim direction.

The nose will be a big black sphere near the front of the head, with a lighter muzzle sphere just below it, and small dark eye spheres positioned symmetrically using left/right offsets calculated so they sit on the sphere's surface. For the ears, I'm placing them toward the top sides of the head using left/right and up offsets with a slight backward pull.

Each ear gets a flat disc shape with its axis along the sideways direction so it reads as a rounded koala ear, plus a smaller cream-colored inner disc nested just inside it for contrast. For the chest, I'm adding a cream sphere positioned along the spine's forward direction to create that classic koala chest patch look.

For fur, I'm layering mottled grey tones with a countershading effect — darker on the back, lighter cream on the belly — applied as a paint texture across the body sweep. Then I'm adding small dark cone-shaped claws at each paw tip, anchored to the foot joints and angled outward from the leg.

Now I'm working out the skeleton proportions: a small stub tail near the hips, a spine chain running from the hip joint up through the neck to the head, and leg sockets positioned so the feet land at ground level with room for the paw spheres and claws.

Feet are little spheres sized and placed so their bottoms sit exactly at the ground, with limb tubes swept along each leg chain tapering toward the tip. I'm figuring out bend directions for the knees and elbows — hind knees bending forward, front elbows bending back — and checking that the hip-to-foot distances fall within the total limb length so the legs can actually reach.

For the spine, I'm making the chain start right at the hips joint so the hips effectively serve as both root and the base of the spine, then naming the subsequent joints spine, chest, and neck — deciding it's fine to keep the naming slightly redundant rather than restructure it. Now I'm working out how the legs should attach, parenting the hind legs to the hips or the nearby spine joint.

I'm mapping each spine joint to its path position so I can parent the shoulders to the chest joint correctly, then defining the body's taper from a wide rump at the hips down to a narrower neck using a radius function along the spine, relying on countershading so the belly naturally reads lighter. For the head, I'm sizing a sphere to match a koala's rounded skull with a cream muzzle tone.

I'm now placing the muzzle, nose, and eyes relative to the head sphere, checking the forward and up offsets so the muzzle sits partly embedded in the head and the nose pokes out just past it without overlapping too much, and sketching rough eye positions and a small highlight sphere for shine.

For the ears I'm working out the distance checks so the ear discs sit just outside the head surface at the top sides, with each ear made of an outer cream disc and a slightly smaller inner disc using mirrored left/right offsets via the `s` sign flip and model-space direction vectors.

Now I'm placing the tail as a small sphere near the hips, checking it protrudes just past the rear body surface, and setting up claw cones on the feet pointing forward using direction vectors so the cone tips aim correctly.

I'm sizing the paw sphere and foot joint height so the paw's bottom just touches the ground instead of sinking in, adjusting the joint target y to 0.04 to compensate.

Now I'm defining leg chains with tapering limb radii, setting up the sweep function for thickness from hip to foot, and building the coat material using a mottled pattern with countershading to separate back and belly tones, plus picking out dark, cream, and accent colors for ears, nose, and eyes.

I'm adding a small white highlight sphere to the eye, checking that it's positioned so it pokes slightly out from the eye surface for a visible glint. Then I'm wiring up the head joint off the neck (third spine joint) with its position and orientation.

Now I'm working out the spine path points and head center so the overall body proportions come out to a realistic standing koala height, confirming the chain's joint indexing lines up correctly with the spine points, and starting to define the body radius profile along the spine.

For the sweep I'll shape rx and ry as functions of t so the body tapers from hips to neck, making sure the neck tube ends inside the head sphere for a seamless join, and deciding to rely on the countershading for the belly rather than adding a separate chest patch. Now I'm working out the limb placement details, naming joints consistently with side-letter suffixes like shoulderL/shoulderR and hipL/hipR, and attaching legs to the appropriate spine joints at chest and hip positions. For the foot/paw endpoint I'm handling the case where the limb's tip might be null by falling back to the last joint in the chain, and avoiding explicit type annotations to keep things simple while passing the limb's returned joint points into the chain constructor.

I'm tallying up the total joint count across spine, head, and four 3-joint limbs to make sure I stay well within budget, then listing out all the visual parts—body sweep, head, muzzle, nose, eyes with highlights, ears with inner/outer discs, paws, claws, leg sweeps, and tail—confirming the part count stays comfortably under the limit. Setting up imports and color palette...

Adding facial features now: nose, eyes with highlights, and ears with outer and inner cylinder shapes positioned symmetrically using the left/forward/up offsets, checking that the inner ear disc pokes through the outer disc for a layered look.

Now I'm setting up the arm and leg chains, building each as a shoulder-elbow-paw sequence with tapered sweep geometry for the limb segments and a sphere at the paw tip, mirroring left and right sides with the sign variable.

I'm adding claws to each paw—small cones positioned forward and splayed left/right at the toe positions—then checking that their placement sits close enough to the ground without clipping through it, adjusting the vertical offset slightly to tuck them under the paw properly.

Now I'm defining the hind legs using the limb helper with appropriate joint offsets, verifying the total limb length stays within the stretch constraint, then adding the tail as a small sphere attached near the hips with enough offset to overlap slightly with the rear body cap so there's no visible gap. I'm placing the eye highlight sphere and deciding to skip extra fur tufts to keep the koala's look simple and stylized, then finishing with the root export and the meta object describing the koala model.
